content.title: About
content.content: Swiss reduced‑fat cheese (536) is a semi‑hard cheese with the characteristic holes, known for its mild nutty flavor. The lower fat content makes it lighter while preserving the traditional texture and aroma of classic Swiss cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Swiss cheese is made from cow’s milk in the Alps.
The holes are created by Propionibacterium bacteria that release carbon dioxide.
Fat reduction is achieved by partially skimming the milk and adding skimmed milk powder.
The cheese is often used in fondue, but the reduced‑fat version melts more quickly.
In the 2020s, demand for reduced‑fat Swiss cheese grew by more than 15 %.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Provides about 800 mg of calcium per 100 g, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Delivers 25 g of high‑quality protein, essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Contains only 10 g of fat per 100 g, helping to control calorie intake.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: Fermentation leaves live cultures that can benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains lactose, so people with intolerance should limit consumption.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is used during aging, so consider this if you follow a low‑sodium diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice thinly for sandwiches, add to salads, use in casseroles, or melt in fondue. It also works well grated over pasta and vegetable dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. For longer storage, the cheese can be frozen for up to 3 months, pre‑sliced into portions.

content.title: About
content.content: Cocktail NFS is a ready‑to‑drink non‑alcoholic beverage made from a blend of fruit juices, berry extracts, and natural flavorings. It contains no artificial colors or preservatives, offers a bright taste and refreshing aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS stands for “Naturally Fresh & Sweet”, highlighting the natural origin of the ingredients.
More than 20 varieties of fruits and berries, harvested at peak ripeness, are used to create its flavor.
The bottle is made from fully recyclable PET plastic, reducing environmental impact.
The drink has low sugar content (no more than 5 g per 100 ml) thanks to the use of stevia as a sweetener.
Each batch is tested for vitamin C levels to ensure freshness of taste.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Fruit juices provide a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Berry extracts are rich in polyphenols that help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: The beverage is mostly water, aiding the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One serving (250 ml) contains about 80 kcal, making it suitable for diet-conscious consumers.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium from the fruit juices helps regulate blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to certain fruits (e.g., citrus) may react to the cocktail.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although low, people with diabetes should monitor their intake.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic pH may contribute to tooth enamel erosion with frequent consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cocktail NFS is best served chilled, straight from the bottle. It can be used as a base for non‑alcoholic mixes, added to smoothies, or enjoyed as a refreshing drink during workouts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, consume within 3‑5 days and keep refrigerated.

content.title: About
content.content: Fish timbale (or fish mousse) is a delicate dish made from fish fillet, eggs, cream and aromatic herbs, baked in small individual molds. The texture can range from firm to airy depending on the recipe.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the French word “timbale”, meaning a baking mold.
It is often served cold as an appetizer at buffets and banquets.
Mousse versions are steamed, giving a lighter, more airy consistency.
Various fish can be used – from tender sea bass to richer salmon.
Traditionally the dish is garnished with micro‑greens, caviar or thin vegetable ribbons.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Fish provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Timbale supplies all essential amino acids for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Fish is a source of selenium, iodine and phosphorus, essential for thyroid health and bones.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes it suitable for low‑carb and keto diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to fish and seafood.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination risk
items.content: Large predatory fish can contain mercury; choose smaller fish or trusted sources.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salty ingredients (e.g., soy sauce) can make the dish overly salty.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking may allow bacterial growth leading to food poisoning.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve the timbale chilled, unmolded, garnished with micro‑greens, caviar, thin vegetable ribbons or a yogurt‑based sauce. It works well as bite‑size appetizers on a platter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the finished timbale in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a separate package for up to 1 month, thawing in the fridge before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: A peanut butter sandwich made with regular peanut butter on white bread is a simple, satisfying snack. The soft bread paired with creamy peanut butter provides a quick source of energy and healthy fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanut butter first appeared in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became popular among athletes.
White bread is often used for sandwiches because its neutral flavor doesn’t overpower the taste of peanut butter.
One sandwich typically contains about 190‑210 kcal, depending on the thickness of the peanut butter layer.
Peanut butter is rich in plant‑based protein, making it a favorite among vegetarians.
Over 1.5 billion peanut butter sandwiches are sold annually in the United States.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Peanut butter contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: A single serving (≈2 tbsp, 32 g) provides about 8 g of plant protein.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Helps stabilize blood sugar
items.content: The combination of protein and fat slows carbohydrate absorption from the bread, preventing sharp glucose spikes.

items.title: Provides magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals support muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are a strong allergen; individuals with a peanut allergy may experience severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Large portions can lead to excess calorie intake and weight gain.

items.title: Added salt and sugar
items.content: Some commercial peanut butter brands contain added salt and sugar, which should be considered in a diet.

items.title: Hydrogenated oils and trans fats
items.content: Certain brands use hydrogenated oils that contain trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread 1‑2 tablespoons of peanut butter evenly on two slices of white bread and press them together. For variety, add banana slices, honey, or jam.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in an airtight container at room temperature for no more than 4 hours. Store opened peanut butter in the refrigerator and keep bread in a dry place.

content.title: About
content.content: Rum is an alcoholic beverage produced by distilling fermented sugarcane by‑products such as molasses, sugarcane juice, or honey. It is traditionally made in tropical regions where sugarcane grows, and its flavor ranges from light and fruity to rich and spicy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest known reference to rum dates back to the 1650s in an English court record.
The word “rum” likely derives from the English slang “rumbullion,” meaning a tumult or uproar.
In the Caribbean, rum served as a de facto currency during the colonial trade era.
There are several rum styles: white, gold, dark, aged, and spiced.
In 1974 the International Spirits Council established a formal classification for rum based on production method and aging.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Some aged rums contain polyphenols that can help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: A small amount of rum after a meal has traditionally been used as a digestif.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: Moderate alcohol consumption may promote relaxation and lower anxiety.

items.title: Alcohol dependence
items.content: Regular consumption of rum can lead to addiction.

items.title: Liver impact
items.content: Excessive alcohol intake damages liver cells and can cause cirrhosis.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Rum may potentiate sedatives and interfere with the efficacy of certain drugs.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Alcohol provides 7 kcal/g, so large servings can contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Rum can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks, or in cocktails such as Mojito, Daiquiri, and Piña Colada. For tasting, use small glasses that allow you to appreciate aroma and flavor. Mixing with fruit juices, cola, or ginger beer creates a wide range of flavor profiles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rum in a tightly sealed bottle, away from direct sunlight and temperature extremes. When kept properly, it can last indefinitely, though its taste may evolve over time.

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato chips are thinly sliced batata pieces that are fried or baked until crisp. They have a naturally sweet flavor, a lightly caramelized aroma, and a crunchy texture. The snack is often marketed as a healthier alternative to regular potato chips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes are richer in beta‑carotene than regular potatoes, giving the chips a bright orange hue.
Compared with traditional chips, sweet potatoes contain more fiber and complex carbohydrates.
Sweet potato chips can be prepared by deep‑frying or oven‑baking, allowing for lower fat versions.
Batata is cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide, including Africa, Southeast Asia, and South America.
Sweet potatoes were domesticated over 5,000 years ago in South America.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact when baked
items.content: Baked sweet potato chips cause a slower rise in blood sugar compared with regular potato chips.

items.title: Provides antioxidants
items.content: Antioxidants protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sweet potato allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience allergic reactions to sweet potato.

items.title: High salt content in flavored versions
items.content: Excessively salty chips can contribute to hypertension; choose low‑salt options when possible.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Fried chips are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Oil degradation at high temperatures
items.content: Cooking at very high heat can produce harmful compounds; use oils with a high smoke point.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sweet potato chips are convenient as a standalone snack, can be tossed into salads, used as a crunchy topping for soups or yogurts, and pair well with dips such as yogurt‑based sauces, guacamole, or hummus.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chips in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent fat oxidation.
